verdict.tagline: Fast fights and constant spam make for a frustrating arena.
for_you_if: you enjoy fast-paced platform fighting action
you want a wide variety of selectable legends and weapons
not_for_you_if: you cannot tolerate server lag and positioning issues
you are easily frustrated by online signature spam
you struggle against unbalanced matchmaking and sweaty opponents

distortion_flags.sentence: Positive ratings rise initially before dropping sharply over extended play times.
Recent reviews score notably lower than the historical lifetime average.

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Players report severe connection issues alongside unbalanced matchmaking and constant heavy attack spam.

claims.claim: Reviewers report issues with lag, server stability, and netcode that causes position swapping.

citations.review_text: Fix your fuck ass shit servers

if you hate your pathetic life and have nothing better to do, play Brawlhalla
we have:
-depression
-fuckers who edge camping
-fuckass netcode for some reason make you swap your position with the enemy
-and your average Ubishit ranked bullshit
and if any of this interest you, congratulation, this is a game for you and if you're keep queuing ranked even after encounter all of those, you probably have stockholm syndrome and you should go get therapy, nevertherless, have "fun" with this shitty ass game if you decided to give it a try.

The chaotic 8-player brawls feel like a sweaty mess of constant knockback spam, and every match turns into a desperate scramble for the edge. With over sixty legends, half of them feel useless against the same few tryhards. Free to play, sure, but the grind and lag ruin the fun.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the matchmaking system as unbalanced, pairing players against opponents with wide skill gaps or resulting in one-sided matches.

citations.review_text: The game is good at first but then as you play a little more, the matchmaking is horrible, making the game almost impossible to progress.

I don't get why the ranked matchmaking is so bad. The players I get are the same in elo but vary wildly in skill. One game I will 3-0 a helpless opponent then lose 0-3 the next game to someone who clearly is not anywhere near the same skill level as the first opponent. How does the ranking system make any sense? I'm not even complaining about losing as I am still ranking up it's just that not having any close games is not an enjoyable experience at all. Not a single game has been close and I have never won or lost 2 in a row. I like the idea of the game I just can't stand playing when either I face a bot or a semi pro player.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience frequent heavy attack or signature spam ('sig spam') by opponents during matches.

citations.review_text: i have never and i mean NEVER have felt this type of rage before and i murder everyone in my area because of these SIG SPAMMERS

before i played this game my life my very happy then my friend asked me to download it i had heard of it before but never played it i joined their private server then his bitch ass decides to sig spam ive broken 2 controllers sence playing this "free" game

Recommended
Honestly, Brawlhalla is a really good game, but the sig spammers make me want to rip my hair out.
The movement and combat feel great, and it's awesome that it's actually free-to-play without any pay-to-win trash. It’s super addictive to just hop on and play.
But matchmaking is literally just fighting people who mash the heavy attack button over and over. It's not that they're impossible to beat, it’s just that playing against it is incredibly boring and frustrating. It ruins the fun of the match.
Play it if you want a great platform fighter, just prepare to lose your sanity to spam.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the movement as snappy and the controls as simple and intuitive to pick up.

citations.review_text: The Addiction PartIt’s stupidly easy to pick up. You jump in, fling people off stages with a spear or gauntlets, and twenty minutes later you’ve somehow spent three hours in ranked. The movement is snappy, the combos feel good when they land, and the “one more game” loop is merciless. There are always new legends, new skins, ranked seasons, and that tiny voice in your head saying “I can still climb out of gold.” Before you know it you’re queuing at 2 a.m. telling yourself this is the last match.It’s the kind of game that doesn’t feel like it demands much… until it owns your free time.The Hate PartAnd yet, almost nobody talks about Brawlhalla without a side of pure venom.The community is infamous. Toxic ranked players, endless “this legend is broken” arguments, and a special brand of salt that only platform fighters can produce. One bad loss and the chat turns into a war crime. Balance patches somehow manage to make half the roster feel unplayable while the other half feels illegal. Matchmaking will gift you the most tilted teammates imaginable, then punish you for existing.People don’t just dislike Brawlhalla. They hate it with the kind of passion usually reserved for broken controllers and people who main the current top legend. It’s the game you uninstall in rage… then reinstall two days later because you’re still thinking about that one match.Final VerdictBrawlhalla is addictive trash. It’s fun, it’s free, it’s competitive, and it will make you question your life choices. It’s the most hated game that somehow keeps millions of people coming back for more punishment.10/10 would get tilted again.

This game gives such a mixed feeling in my mind. I really wish I could recommend this game to new players. Unfortunately, Brawlhalla as it exists (as far as I can tell for the predictable future) has become such a mixed bag that in my opinion the cons outweigh the pros for recommending anyone new to the game. 

For full disclosure, I have earned every character in the game with in-game currency, the only items I have bought for this game is a single taunt (worth around $5). I also bought the all-characters pack for ps4 because I refused to grind the entire roster out a second time. 


I have played this game since the 2010s when the roster was about 10 characters and dashing didn't even exist in the game. I obviously enjoy the gameplay, apparent by my around 800+ hours of time spent since leaving this review. Unfortunately, I have also watched the game's development company completely forget the game it used to be and focus almost exclusively on new characters and weapons that outclass every one of the original characters they have forgotten existed in the roster. They have also altered the primary art direction so drastically that any of the original visual clarity in the game has been painted over with bright neons and cluttery clashing color palettes.

When this game is played casually, it is an absolute blast. Character movement flows smoothly and the basic controls are fairly simple and intuitive to pick up for newcomers after about a couple hours of playing. Brawlhalla excels at creating a welcoming environment for personal games with friends. Where things begin to go astray is once you start attempting to climb the skill ladder in ranked play.  

Brawlhalla's movement tech and more advanced move sets are not explained to the new player until they either search around the main menu and find the tutorials (that I never knew existed until well over 500 hours into gameplay) or you look up tutorials on the internet. Otherwise, you will be completely outma…

single_points.text: One reviewer states that matchmaking is trash and that wins net you morsels while losses destroy your ELO.

citation.review_text: I stopped playing this game was when Onyx came out because my Xbox broke. I remembered playing this with my sibling, loving the character designs and having so much fun with it. When I finally having came back to the game when Arcadia was introduced I had fun with the game, playing free for all until I thought I was good enough to do 1v1s. I started playing Strikeout, which became my favourite game mode. I got better and better, I even fought against high plat and low diamond players and convincingly won a lot of those games. Then slowly the fan base became one of the most fucked up assortment of creatures I dread to call human beings. I 3 stock a guy playing his main three in strikeout, mind you I'm playing randomised legends to train at the game, he beats me narrowly, invites me to a private lobby and calls me trash, even though I 3 stock him last game, and leaves. Some while after this, I took a break from the game. When I came back, these braindead homunculi got worse somehow. I persisted, got better at the game and said "Let's try ranked.", I'm sad to say the experience is just awful, horrible, atrocious, downright devious, if you will. Wins net you morsels and losses destroy your ELO. Tell me why, when I've beaten three players significantly above 1700 ELO, why am I still at 1500-1600 ELO, when I started at low 1500. Not to mention that the matchmaking is trash. Does it even account for players maximum rank, if it does the system doesn't work, if it doesn't just why. The game's trash don't spend your time on this.
